entities.evidence: The verse names Pishon as the first of the four river branches and identifies it by its course around Havilah.
The phrase “land of Havilah” names the territory around which the Pishon flows and where the gold is. The source tag identifies this place with the Genesis 2:11 bearer.

review.translation: [The name of|0] [the first|1] {is} [Pishon|2]. [It|3] {is} [the one that winds around|4] [the whole|5,6] [land of|7] [Havilah|8], [where|9,10] [the gold|11] {is}.

analysis.evidence: שֵׁם הָאֶחָד means “the name of the first [river].” פִּישׁוֹן supplies that name.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: name by which someone is known

analysis.evidence: שֵׁם הָאֶחָד פִּישׁוֹן means “the name of the first is Pishon.” The numeral identifies the first river in the sequence.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + cardinal numeral, masculine singular absolute, used substantivally with ordinal force.
analysis.sense: first (in a count, and of dates)

draft.change: Add a geographical proper noun under its own consonantal spelling. The passage gives no derivation for the name.
draft.definition: Pishon is the river that goes around the whole land of Havilah.
draft.evidence: Genesis 2:11 explicitly names Pishon and identifies its course.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 2:10 describes a river dividing into four branches. In 2:11, שֵׁם הָאֶחָד פִּישׁוֹן gives the name of the first branch. The masculine singular הוּא הַסֹּבֵב resumes the river as the subject and identifies it by its course around Havilah.
analysis.morphology: Geographical proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: The first of the four river branches from Eden, which goes around the land of Havilah.

analysis.evidence: הוּא refers back to פִּישׁוֹן and serves as the subject of הוּא הַסֹּבֵב, “it is the one that goes around.” The following phrase identifies Havilah as the land the river encircles.
analysis.morphology: Independent personal pronoun, third person masculine singular.

analysis.evidence: הוּא refers back to the Pishon. The participle describes the river’s course, and אֵת marks כָּל־אֶרֶץ הַחֲוִילָה, “the whole land of Havilah,” as its direct object.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, with prefixed definite article הַ־.

analysis.evidence: אֵת introduces כָּל אֶרֶץ הַחֲוִילָה, “the whole land of Havilah,” as the object of הַסֹּבֵב, “which encircles.” The phrase identifies what the Pishon encircles.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֵת כָּל אֶרֶץ הַחֲוִילָה, כָּל marks the full extent of a single territory. The Pishon circles the whole land of Havilah.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל אֶרֶץ הַחֲוִילָה, “the whole land of Havilah,” אֶרֶץ stands in construct with the place name Havilah and denotes the territory that the Pishon encircles.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, singular construct, without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add the geographical name חֲוִילָה under its own consonants. The verse supplies no evidence for a derivation from חוט or for the gloss “sweat.”
draft.definition: Havilah is the land around which the Pishon flows in Genesis 2:11.
draft.evidence: Genesis 2:11 names Havilah after אֶרֶץ, “land,” and locates gold there.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל אֶרֶץ הַחֲוִילָה, “the whole land of Havilah,” the name identifies the land around which the Pishon flows. The relative clause אֲשֶׁר שָׁם הַזָּהָב, “where the gold is,” describes that land.
analysis.morphology: Geographical proper noun with prefixed definite article הַ־.
analysis.sense: The land around which the Pishon flows.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause modifying אֶרֶץ הַחֲוִילָה, “the land of Havilah.” Within the clause, שָׁם (“there”) refers back to the land, so אֲשֶׁר שָׁם הַזָּהָב means “where the gold is.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֲשֶׁר שָׁם הַזָּהָב, “where the gold is,” שָׁם points back to the land of Havilah and locates the gold there.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected adverb of place with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The clause אֲשֶׁר שָׁם הַזָּהָב, “where the gold is,” identifies gold as a material found in the land of Havilah.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute common noun with prefixed definite article הַ־.
